posture.statement: Kana Sprint starts on the playable game surface and keeps N5-N1 mastery progress, daily run goals, run missions, weak-item review, local data reset, language, music, support/privacy, rewarded-ad, daily challenge, and exit controls reachable from runtime UI.
posture.releaseAction: If this audit fails, fix the runtime App.tsx flow before regenerating screenshots or submitting for review.

checks.label: First screen is a playable ready state with practice and daily challenge entry points
evidence: App.tsx initializes phase to ready and renders practice/daily buttons from the ready body.

checks.label: N5-N1 difficulty selector is sourced from the study-bank level list and shows real counts
evidence: 5 JLPT levels exposed: N5, N4, N3, N2, N1.

checks.label: Ready screen shows local mastery progress for every JLPT level
evidence: The ready screen renders N5-N1 progress rows from the local mastery store.

checks.label: Ready screen exposes a local weak-item review loop from recent mistakes
evidence: Recent wrong answers are persisted locally, filtered by mode/level, and replayed through a dedicated weak-review entry.

checks.label: Ready screen recommends the next local learning action from weak items and JLPT mastery
evidence: The ready screen turns local mastery and mistake data into a tappable next-step recommendation.

checks.label: Ready screen shows local achievement milestones from runs, streaks, mastery, and N1 progress
evidence: The ready screen adds compact local achievement badges without accounts, analytics, or server sync.

checks.label: Each run has a visible local mission target, live progress text, and finish-state result
evidence: A lightweight run mission is generated from mode/level/daily-review context, shown before play, updated during play, and resolved on the finish screen.

checks.label: Ready screen shows a persisted daily run goal that advances after every finished run
evidence: The ready screen renders today's local run target and storage advances/resets it by date without accounts or server sync.

checks.label: Five game modes are exposed before a run: mix, kana, words, lines, and grammar
evidence: 5 modes found in App.tsx: mix, kana, vocab, lines, grammar.

checks.label: Playing state contains timer, score, combo/lives, prompt, four options, feedback, and answer handling
evidence: The playing branch wires score/timer UI to answerQuestion and scoreForAnswer.

checks.label: Answered questions reveal a compact study hint with the correct answer, reading, and meaning
evidence: The playing branch keeps the answer reveal visible long enough to show reading, romaji, and localized meaning after each answer.

checks.label: A visible in-game exit button returns from an active run to the ready screen
evidence: The playing header uses the localized exitRun button and the goHome handler resets to ready.

checks.label: Finished state lets the player play again or switch mode without restarting the app
evidence: The finished branch exposes play-again and switch-mode flows.

checks.label: Finished state summarizes new mastery and mistakes, then links back into weak review
evidence: The finish screen turns the just-finished run into a learning recap and a direct review path for misses.

checks.label: Language switching lives inside Settings, follows the system by default, and excludes Japanese as a UI locale
evidence: 10 settings locales found; Japanese UI locale present: no.

checks.label: Settings exposes a two-tap local progress reset without accounts or server sync
evidence: The Settings modal resets only the local progress object after an explicit confirmation tap.

checks.label: Settings exposes support, privacy, open-source notices, and ad privacy options when available
evidence: Support, privacy, open-source, local fallback information, and UMP ad privacy entries are only in Settings.

checks.label: Settings exposes BGM enablement and track selection without adding recording permissions
evidence: 3 BGM tracks configured: rush, focus, night.

checks.label: Rewarded-ad continue entry is wired from gameplay UI to native/web ad boundaries
evidence: The gameplay ad button calls claimAdReward; native and web ad boundary files exist.

checks.label: Daily challenge and streak state are retained locally across sessions
evidence: Daily challenge keys are level-aware in App.tsx and streak state is persisted by storage.ts.

checks.label: Runtime flow stays no-account/local-first while still exposing review-ready links and ad entry points
evidence: No TextInput, sign-in, or auth entry appears in App.tsx; progress/settings stay local.
